propositions: A bare repository fixture created with `git init --bare` and then pushed into leaves a detached `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` background process that outlives the push, causing concurrent mutation of the object database.

The immediately-subsequent `shutil.copytree` walk races against git repacking loose-object fanout directories into packfiles, causing `shutil.Error` when the walk encounters deleted entries (not limited to `objects/maintenance.lock`).

Pinning `receive.autogc=false`, `gc.autoDetach=false`, and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` on a bare fixture remote before any push removes the detached background mutator entirely, converting the concurrent race into a sequential operation.

The fix is verified by a new test that runs the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, confirms `git receive-pack` was invoked (positive control), and asserts no `git maintenance run` child carries the `--detach` flag.
Filtering `*.lock` entries or retrying the copytree would tolerate the race rather than eliminate it, leaving the repack window open and producing rarer, harder-to-diagnose flakes.
